findings.quote: Q₂ = mL = 20000 g × 80 cal g⁻¹ = 800000 cal
findings.note: The mass is 10 kg = 10000 g, not 20000 g - the same mass the previous step correctly used as 10000 g - and the printed product is false on its own terms as well, since 20000 × 80 = 1600000, not 800000. A student copying this line either doubles the mass or accepts a wrong multiplication, and gets 1600000 + 50000 = 1650000 cal = 693 × 10⁴ J, which matches no option. The final answer is right only because the printed result 800000 cal is the value the correct mass gives.
findings.fix: Q₂ = mL = 10000 g × 80 cal g⁻¹ = 800000 cal

question_defect: The specific heat capacity of ice is printed as "0.5 cal g⁻¹", which is the unit of a latent heat; a specific heat capacity needs the per-degree factor, cal g⁻¹ °C⁻¹. The solution silently supplies the missing °C⁻¹ in its own first line.
notes: Solved independently first: Q1 = 10000 g × 0.5 × 10 = 50000 cal, Q2 = 10000 g × 80 = 800000 cal, total 850000 cal × 4.2 J/cal = 3570000 J = 357 × 10⁴ J, option 1. Confirmed with python. Both common_mistakes entries are numerically correct and point at the right options: reading 10 kg as 1 kg gives 85000 cal = 357000 J = 357 × 10³ J (option 2), and reading it as 100 kg gives 8500000 cal = 35700000 J = 357 × 10⁵ J (option 4). The 1 cal = 4.2 J conversion is the one the options require - 4.186 would give 3558000 J, which still rounds to the same option - so it is not a finding. Every other printed line is correct; the single defect is the mass written in step 2.
